subject: Post-demo: ClearLedger integration — auth pattern proposal & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearledger.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: ClearLedger integration — auth pattern proposal & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Short recap + recommended next steps from our side so we can unblock an integration POC quickly.

Quick recap
- Goal: Replace a portion of ClearLedger's rule engine calls with Redwood-hosted inference for structured summary + reranker pipeline.
- Primary concerns you raised: key management, rotation, auditability (who called what and when), and support for short-lived tokens for client-side tooling.

Redwood recommended auth approach (phased):
1) POC phase (fastest): scoped API keys issued from a dedicated ClearLedger project in Redwood. Keys will be limited to the POC model and IP-restricted to your VPC egress.
2) Pre-prod: move to JWT service-account flow (client obtains short-lived JWT via your identity provider -> exchange for Redwood short-lived token). This enables per-service identity, tighter rotation cadence, and easier audit binding.
3) Prod: pair service accounts with KMS/HSM-encrypted secrets and automatic rotation (we support AWS KMS / GCP KMS / HashiVault integration).

Implementation notes / integration checklist (high level)
- SDK bootstrapping: we provide a small starter repo (Node + Python) that handles token exchange and retry logic.
- Key rotation: suggest 30-day rotation for long-lived POC keys, move to 1-hour TTL for exchanged tokens during pre-prod.
- Routing: recommend canary route to Redwood Dedicated pool for the first 10% of traffic, fallback to hosted model variants on errors.
- Structured output & tool-calling: we'll surface function/tool-calling in the SDK; suggest tests that assert schema (JSON schema) for summaries before ingest into your system.
- Embeddings/rerankers: embeddings should be computed in a dedicated batch job with unique embedding keys tied to service account; reranker config pinned to model version in Redwood Console.

Next steps I propose (actionable):
- You: confirm who will own the API key/service-account creation on ClearLedger's side (ops@clearledger.com is fine).
- Us: spin up POC project + issue two scoped API keys (read-only inference + rerank) and share via secure DocuSign-style link.
- Joint: schedule 60m integration session next Tue to walk SDK onboarding and token exchange flow.

Attachments: integration checklist, service-account template, and a short rotation guidance doc.

If that looks good I can open the POC project and create the keys tomorrow.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment stubs: redwood-integration-checklist.csv (CSV), svc-account-template.json (JSON), example-rotation-schedule.md (MD)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearledger.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T17:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearLedger integration — auth pattern proposal & next steps

Thanks Soojin — that plan is clear and aligns with our security ask. A couple of clarifying items before we move keys around:

1) Audit/logging: we need per-token and per-request audit logs that include a request id and the full model version used. Do you expose token-level logs in the Console and can we ship them to our logging endpoint?
2) Rotation + vault: we prefer automated rotation via our HashiCorp Vault instance. Can Redwood rotate the initial POC keys on-demand (if we trigger rotation from Vault) or do we need to delete/create a new key from your Console each time?
3) SOC2 artifacts: can you share the standard SOC2 summary + penetration test cadence doc to pass to our InfoSec?

Ops will own provisioning (ops@clearledger.com). Let’s tentatively keep Tue 07/23 11:00 PT for the integration session. Ben — looping you in to confirm the canary routing and token TTL support.

— Elena
Elena Ruiz
VP Engineering | ClearLedger
elena@clearledger.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearledger.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearLedger integration — auth pattern proposal & next steps

Elena — quick answers:
- Audit/logging: yes, Redwood Console provides per-request traces with model version, request id, and token id. We can stream those logs to your endpoint (via HTTPS webhook or S3 push) and include a daily digest.
- Vault rotation: we support a rotation API that Vault can call to rotate keys. For POC keys we can enable on-demand rotate/delete through API; no manual Console steps required. For long-lived service accounts we recommend the JWT exchange (Vault issues signed JWT -> Redwood exchange).
- SOC2: Soojin will attach the SOC2 summary and pen-test cadence in the follow-up.

On canary routing: we can configure 10% of calls to route to Redwood Dedicated with automatic fallback. We'll include traffic metrics and latency SLOs in the canary dashboard. For TTLs: we support TTLs down to 5 minutes for exchanged tokens.

I’ll provision the POC project and two keys once ops confirms the owner email.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@clearledger.com>, ops@clearledger.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ClearLedger integration — auth pattern proposal & next steps

Perfect — thanks all. Confirming agreed action items and owners: 
- Ops (ops@clearledger.com): create ClearLedger project in your Vault and confirm the admin email for POC key provisioning. (Due: 2028-07-21)
- Redwood (Ben / Soojin): provision POC project & two scoped API keys; enable rotation API endpoint for your Vault. We will deliver keys via secure share and enable IP restriction. (Due: 2028-07-21)
- Joint: Integration session Tue 2028-07-23 11:00 PT — agenda will cover SDK onboarding, token exchange demo, and canary routing verification. I’ll send a calendar invite.
- Security artifacts: attaching SOC2 summary + pen-test cadence + the templates mentioned earlier.

If ops confirms ownership I’ll create the POC project tomorrow morning and share the secure key delivery link.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
